[The numbered gates on the connectors – deployment registration, expert verification, AI benchmarking, standards conformance – are what MANTIS adds. Most of what lies either side of them already exists in Europe.]{.section-lede}

## What the activity does

**Connect data acquisition** – align protocols, deployments and annotations across partners. Extend spatial and taxonomic coverage with new sensor deployments. [Package 1 · seven activities · Core Activity 2]{.quiet}

**Connect the data** – harmonise datasets and metadata. Ensure flow from images and sounds to quality-controlled indicators, including transnational benchmarking of AI models. [Package 2 · five activities · Core Activity 3, primary]{.quiet}

**Connect the community** – link the users of these technologies to one another, and to the skills and resources that sustain a transnational effort. [Package 3 · seven activities · Core Activity 4]{.quiet}

[Nineteen activities in all, with nine deliverables and sixteen milestones between 1 January 2027 and 30 September 2028. MANTIS could develop into a Thematic Hub associated with an EBOCC. It sets up no new operational structure: outputs are hosted on GitHub Pages, GBIF and Zenodo, and verification capacity rests on statutory Habitats and Birds Directive duties.]{.section-lede}

## Objectives and deadlines

| | Target and indicator | Deadline |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **O1** Deployment registration | 100% of active AMI, CamAlien and acoustic deployments across ≥8 partner countries, registered and machine-readable in a Camtrap DP-compliant master database | 30 Sep 2028 |
| **O2** Policy-relevant indicators | ≥4 finalised indicators live on the MANTIS dashboard, each mapped to NRR Art. 10 / EU-PoMS, the Habitats Directive, the Birds Directive or IAS Regulation 1143/2014, and auto-updating from GBIF | 30 Sep 2028 |
| **O3** Verified annotations | ≥5,000 expert-verified annotations published under FAIR principles, including ≥2,000 NewtCam annotations; ≥20% reviewed by experts from ≥2 countries | 31 Dec 2027 |
| **O4** Training | 25 summer-school participants from ≥12 countries; ≥20 distinct organisations attending ≥1 of the 8 online events | 30 Jun 2028 |
| **O5** Roadmap beyond 2028 | Roadmap endorsed by ≥2/3 of partners at BioMonWeek 2028, naming ≥2 concrete funding or hosting pathways | 30 Jun 2028 |

## The devices, in the field

[Three device families: AMI traps for nocturnal insects, acoustic recorders for birds, bats and amphibians, and the vehicle-mounted CamAlien for invasive plants along roads. These are existing partner deployments, which MANTIS would register, upgrade and benchmark.]{.section-lede}

```{=html}

<img class="gallery__media" src="images/gallery/ami-trap-grassland.jpg" alt="An AMI trap deployed in dry grassland: a white weatherproof enclosure and a solar panel standing inside a fenced enclosure of tall grass.">
<figcaption><span class="gallery__kicker">AMI trap</span>A camera trap for nocturnal insects, running unattended on solar power in dry grassland. Activity 1.4 retrofits deployments like this one with modems and SIM cards so health checks and image transfer happen remotely instead of by field visit.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure class="gallery__item">
<img class="gallery__media" src="images/gallery/ami-sheet-night.jpg" alt="A close view of an illuminated white sheet covered with dozens of moths, craneflies and small insects photographed by an automated camera at night.">
<figcaption><span class="gallery__kicker">One frame, one night</span>An illuminated sheet, photographed at intervals through the night. The volume of images like this has outgrown the capacity to verify them.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure class="gallery__item">

<figcaption><span class="gallery__kicker">Acoustic recorders</span>Song Meter units at a meadow edge, recording audible and ultrasound. Many deployed recorders still need a field visit to retrieve data. Activity 1.4 upgrades them for solar power and cellular remote access.</figcaption>

<figure class="gallery__item">

<figcaption><span class="gallery__kicker">CamAlien</span>A high-speed, car-mounted camera system with automated image capture and GPS processing. Roads are a key route for the spread of invasive alien species. Mapping plants along them supports early detection under IAS Regulation 1143/2014.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure class="gallery__item">
<img class="gallery__media" src="images/gallery/camalien-camera.jpg" alt="Close view of the CamAlien rig: a lens in a black housing beside a white weatherproof control box, strapped to a roof bar.">
<figcaption><span class="gallery__kicker">The rig up close</span>Lens, housing and control box on the roof bar. Activity 1.4 installs new onboard computers and GPS, so images can be classified on the vehicle in real time.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure class="gallery__item">
<img class="gallery__media gallery__media--fit" src="images/gallery/ai-verification-ui.jpg" alt="A screenshot of an annotation interface: a scatterplot of insect crops, a list of taxonomic labels such as Araneae and Coleoptera, and a gallery panel showing two moths enlarged for review.">
<figcaption><span class="gallery__kicker">Expert verification</span>Experts review AI-proposed identifications to build the reference dataset used for benchmarking – at least 5,000 verified annotations, a fifth of them checked in two countries, by the end of 2027.</figcaption>
</figure>
```
